targets.name: User temporary files
targets.description: Temporary files left behind by apps and installers (%TEMP%). Files in use are skipped.

targets.name: Windows temporary files
targets.description: System-wide temporary folders (C:\Windows\Temp and service account temp folders).

targets.name: Recycle Bin
targets.description: Files you already deleted. Emptying it makes them unrecoverable.

targets.name: Windows Update cache
targets.description: Downloaded update packages that are already installed. Windows re-downloads if needed.

targets.name: Delivery Optimization cache
targets.description: Update pieces cached to share with other PCs.

targets.name: Windows Installer patch cache
targets.description: Baseline copies of patched files ($PatchCache$). Microsoft documents it as safe to delete; some very old patches may ask for the original media when uninstalled.

targets.name: System memory dumps
targets.description: Minidumps and live kernel reports written after blue screens and driver hangs.

targets.name: Full memory dump (MEMORY.DMP)
targets.description: The full crash dump from the last blue screen. Can be as large as your RAM; only useful for debugging that crash.

targets.name: Windows error reports
targets.description: Crash and problem reports already sent (or queued) to Microsoft.

targets.name: App crash dumps
targets.description: Memory dumps created when apps crash. Only useful for debugging.

targets.name: Windows setup & servicing logs
targets.description: CBS/DISM log files and their archives. These can grow to several GB on some PCs.

targets.name: Thumbnail cache
targets.description: Explorer picture previews. Rebuilt automatically when folders are opened.

targets.name: Previous Windows installation (Windows.old)
targets.description: Left after a Windows upgrade. Removing it means you can no longer roll back to the previous version.

targets.name: Windows upgrade temporary files
targets.description: $Windows.~BT, $Windows.~WS, ESD, $GetCurrent, $SysReset and $WinREAgent folders left by feature updates, resets or the Media Creation Tool. Don't clean while an upgrade is in progress.

targets.name: Old Office installation source (MSOCache)
targets.description: Local copy of old Office 2007–2013 setup files. Office keeps working; repairing it may ask for the installation media.

targets.name: Graphics driver installer leftovers
targets.description: Extracted NVIDIA/AMD/Intel driver installers (C:\NVIDIA, C:\AMD, downloader caches). Installed drivers are not affected.

targets.name: Browser caches
targets.description: Cached web content for Chrome, Edge, Brave, Vivaldi, Opera and Firefox. Logins, history and bookmarks are kept. Close browsers first.

targets.name: Website offline storage (Service Worker cache)
targets.description: Offline copies saved by websites and web apps. Often several GB; sites simply re-download what they need.

targets.name: Chat & collaboration app caches
targets.description: Discord, Slack and Microsoft Teams caches. Messages stay on the server; close the apps first.

targets.name: Telegram Desktop media cache
targets.description: Photos, videos and files Telegram cached while you scrolled chats (often many GB). They re-download from Telegram when opened. Close Telegram first.

targets.name: Spotify cache
targets.description: Streamed songs cached by Spotify (can reach 10 GB). Downloaded playlists for offline listening may need to be re-downloaded.

targets.name: iPhone / iPad software update files
targets.description: iOS firmware files (.ipsw, 5–8 GB each) downloaded by iTunes or Apple Devices. Downloaded again if you update through the PC.

targets.name: Microsoft Office document cache
targets.description: Office's upload/sync cache for OneDrive and SharePoint files. Close Office apps first; unsynced changes should be saved beforehand.

targets.name: Adobe media cache
targets.description: Premiere Pro / After Effects media cache files. Rebuilt when projects are reopened (the first open is slower).

targets.name: VS Code caches
targets.description: Visual Studio Code web caches and downloaded extension installers. Settings and extensions are kept.

targets.name: GPU shader caches
targets.description: DirectX / NVIDIA / AMD / Intel shader caches. Games may stutter briefly while rebuilding.

targets.name: Steam caches
targets.description: Steam's downloaded shader pre-caches, web browser cache and leftover update files. Games and saves are not touched. Close Steam first.

targets.name: Game launcher caches
targets.description: Epic Games, EA app, Ubisoft Connect, Battle.net and GOG Galaxy web caches and logs.

targets.name: Unreal Engine / Unity caches
targets.description: Derived data and asset caches for game development. Rebuilt automatically; the next project open is slower.

targets.name: npm / Yarn / Bun / Deno caches
targets.description: Downloaded JavaScript packages. Projects keep working; packages are re-downloaded on the next install.

targets.name: NuGet download caches
targets.description: NuGet HTTP and plugin caches (not the global packages folder).

targets.name: NuGet global packages
targets.description: All restored .NET packages (%USERPROFILE%\.nuget\packages). Often many GB; restored again on the next build, which needs internet.

targets.name: pip / uv / Poetry caches
targets.description: Downloaded Python wheels and packages. Existing environments keep working.

targets.name: JetBrains IDE caches
targets.description: Index and system caches for IntelliJ, Rider, PyCharm, WebStorm, Android Studio... Rebuilt on next start (first indexing is slower).

targets.name: Scoop / Chocolatey download caches
targets.description: Installer files kept after apps were installed with Scoop or Chocolatey. Installed apps are not affected.

targets.name: Gradle / Maven / Go / Cargo caches
targets.description: Build and dependency caches for Java/Android, Go and Rust. Rebuilt or re-downloaded on the next build.

targets.name: AI model caches (Hugging Face / PyTorch)
targets.description: Downloaded machine-learning models, often 5–50 GB. Scripts download them again when needed, which can take a long time.

targets.name: Conda package cache
targets.description: Downloaded package archives for Anaconda / Miniconda. Environments keep working; same as 'conda clean --all'.

targets.name: Android emulator system images
targets.description: Android SDK system images (1–3 GB each). Emulators using them stop working until you re-download them in Android Studio.

targets.name: Downloads folder
targets.description: Everything in your Downloads folder. May contain personal files — review before cleaning.

targets.name: iPhone / iPad backups
targets.description: Local device backups made by iTunes or Apple Devices. Often tens of GB. Deleting them removes your only copy unless you also back up to iCloud.
